_doc: SILENT CATCHES — every `catch` of `src/` that reports to no journal, DECLARED with its count and its reason (2026-10-04). DETECTION is `rules/no-silent-catch.yml` (ast-grep, no exemption); POLICY and RATCHET are `test/silent-catch-gate.test.js`. A file absent from this list is held at ZERO: a new silent `catch` is RED until it calls `log.hookError` / `log.daemonError` / `log.write`, or is declared here with why its silence is the right answer.
_doc_why: A hook or a daemon that swallows an error leaves NOTHING: the harness sees exit 0 and the failure is invisible for as long as nobody suspects it. Measured the day this gate was born: after the journal writer existed, 9 of 12 hooks still swallowed in silence. A silence is legitimate only when the caught case IS the expected answer (an absent config means the defaults, an already-removed file is the desired end state) or when reporting is impossible (the journal writer itself, a module the writer depends on).
_doc_ratchet: EQUALITY, both directions: more catches than declared is RED (a new silence nobody judged), fewer is RED too (a dormant permit the next silence would inherit). Lower the count in the same commit that removes a silence.
_doc_perimeter: `src/` only, stated: it is what runs unattended. `tools/` and `service/` are commands the operator launches; their failures land on the operator's own terminal (named refusals, exit codes), which is the right channel for them.

src/cadence-spec.js.why: The independent cadence MODEL decodes a JSON-looking value; a value that is not JSON is simply not decoded (undefined), which is the semantics under test, not a failure.

src/collect-core.js.why: `loadConfig`: an absent or unreadable config means the framework defaults, by contract of every reader here; reporting it would write a line on every clean install.

src/commit-msg-leak.js.why: The optional personal-data guard is absent on a contributor's machine; null is the documented 'generic mode' and the commit gate says which mode it ran in.

src/corpus-cache.js.why: Closing a watcher that is already closed is the desired end state; a failed cache arm answers null, which makes the caller read the disk exactly as without a cache (no loss, only speed).

src/deadline.js.why: The deadline's last-gasp rendering: the hook is being killed on purpose, the output takes precedence, and the journal writer cannot be trusted inside a dying process.

src/deployed-scan.js.why: A file absent on one side of the comparison stays null, and null is the verdict `drift` the doctor reports by name; the absence IS the measured fact, not a lost error.

src/doctor-wiring-pure.js.why: Pure reader of the settings for the doctor: a non-ENOENT error is returned as a named `detail` the doctor prints, ENOENT is the retried absence; nothing is swallowed, it is answered.

src/frontmatter.js.why: Scalar parsing of a frontmatter value: a value that is not JSON is kept as the raw text, which is the documented reading of the format, not a failure.

src/guard-core.js.why: One unreadable or just-deleted doc path is skipped so the others are still validated; the whole-run failure of this guard IS journalled (the outer catch).

src/hooks/canary-check.js.why: A transcript that cannot be stat'ed is recorded as size -1 ('not measurable', never 0) in the canary's own observation log, which is the channel that reports it.

src/hooks/daemon-ensure.js.why: Each failed probe leaves its status null, and null IS the result: the pure decision reads it as `unmeasured` and stays silent by design (a security suite pausing the task is routine, never an alarm).

src/hooks/http-server.js.why: Runtime capability probes that answer null when the runtime does not expose the measure (event-loop histogram, somaxconn) · an unparseable identity that defers to `handle`, which journals it · destroying a socket already gone (three sites, the desired end state) · a failed re-arm handed to `onCannotRearm`, which records `watch-lost` · a state-dir mkdir the bind reports next · and three lines whose own journal write failed, where reporting would be a journal about the journal.

src/hooks/legacy-mcp-inject.js.why: The FROZEN differential oracle, never wired: its doc forbids it any evolution, because the differentials compare the engine against this exact code.

src/hooks/session-inject.js.why: An absent or unreadable config means the framework defaults (framework active), like every other reader; the hook's own failure path IS journalled.

src/hooks/state-client.js.why: An unparseable daemon answer becomes `finish(null)`, and every caller treats null as 'no daemon answer' with its own documented fallback (the turn counter even tells the human).

src/hooks/state-owner-thread.js.why: A throw in an owner operation is ANSWERED to the waiting client as an error slot, never swallowed and never left pending; the client side carries it.

src/hooks/turn-count.js.why: An absent or unreadable config means the framework defaults (framework active), like every other reader; the hook's own failure paths ARE journalled.

src/hooks/wrap-up-observe.js.why: An absent or unreadable config means the option is off, which is the documented default; the hook's own failure paths ARE journalled.

src/hooks/wrap-up-stop.js.why: An unreadable message file falls back to the default message AND tells the human in the same answer · a report already evicted by another process is the desired end state · an absent config means the option is off.

src/hooks/wrap-up-touch.js.why: An absent or unreadable config means the option is off, which is the documented default; the hook's own failure paths ARE journalled.

src/judge-runner.js.why: Killing a judge tree the kernel already reaped is the desired end state · a spawn failure is answered as `spawnError`, which `verdictOf` reads as `broken` and the human is told by name.

src/kernel-bind.js.why: Removing a dead socket entry another instance already removed is the benign race; any other code is rethrown to the bind, which reports it.

src/leak-list.js.why: The private leak list is absent on a public clone: the gate then runs in its documented generic mode and says so; inventing a list would be worse.

src/lifecycle-log.js.why: The door of the daemon journal itself: a failure to write a journal line cannot be written to that journal.

src/lock.js.why: `log.js` depends on this module (the rotation lock), so a journal call here would be a require cycle. Its catches are either kernel answers that ARE the protocol (ESRCH proof of death, EPERM alive, transient codes retried, a lock already released) or its fail-open, whose cost each caller documents.

src/log.js.why: The journal writer itself: an unreadable config means the defaults, an absent generation means nothing to shift, and a failed write cannot be journalled by the journal.

src/memory-store.js.why: Removing a temporary file that was never written is the desired end state; the lost snapshot SAVE and the unreadable snapshot LOAD are both journalled.

src/oracle.js.why: The frozen protect-files oracle of the differential: its behaviour is the reference and may not evolve.

src/paths.js.why: Reading an optional key of an absent or unreadable config returns undefined, i.e. the code-derived default; an invalid DECLARED value is a named refusal elsewhere in this module.

src/response-pure.js.why: A tool answer that is not JSON stays text, which is the documented reading of the `response` filter, not a failure.

src/session-store.js.why: The read-through answers ENOENT as an absence it retries and returns `{}` on a real error by contract · listing probes answer 'no write in flight' · each rename attempt keeps its error for the report made once the retries are exhausted · removing a temporary already gone. The two LOST-WRITE paths ARE journalled.

src/source-adapters.js.why: An unreadable skill file falls back to the pointer injection, which tells the agent where the skill lives; the three source-wide failures ARE journalled.

src/split-scope-pure.js.why: A hasher that throws yields the empty signature, which matches nothing, so the action is split as before: fails towards more work, never towards wrong frames (documented).

src/stale-code.js.why: A recorded module that is gone or unreadable is reported as GONE in the verdict, which makes the daemon exit 90 and record `stale-code-exit` with the reason.

src/state-eviction.js.why: No state directory yet (fresh install) · a file removed between listing and stat · a file held by another process: the next sweep retries, and the refused DECISION is journalled.

src/stdin-json.js.why: The parse error is handed to the caller's `onError`, and every hook's `onError` journals it; this standalone utility may depend on nothing.

src/wrap-up-pure.js.why: A judge output that is not JSON is read as raw text, which is the documented judge contract (text or JSON), not a failure.
